title: Frontend garage brainstorm standup — 2026-06-14
content:
Attendees: Priya, Marcus, Rina, Liam, Jae (quick drop-ins from Analytics and SRE)

Purpose: short garage-style standup to surface blockers and rapid ideas for the next 48h. Focus: rollout gating UX, lightweight canary telemetry in the panel, and a small experiment to reduce p95 token latency for preview flows.

Notes / stream-of-consciousness captures:
- Quick wins: Marcus wired up the minimal canary panel widget (see PR #482). It renders canary success:failure counts and exposes a toggle to narrow to a model variant. UI skeleton done but needs plumbing to event schema.
- Telemetry gap: current telemetry schema doesn't include route-level rollout tags (we only have model_id + deployment_id). Analytics needs "rollout_cohort" string so we can join UI events -> canary cohorts. Rina to file schema change (INF-2411).
- UX question: how should we show automated fallback behavior in the rollout timeline? Two options: inline banner showing last fallback with timestamp vs. an expandable timeline entry. Quick poll: inline banner is preferable for on-call visibility, timeline for post-mortem reading. Plan: MVP banner + link to timeline.
- Cost signal: João from infra flagged spike in token-cost for preview endpoints during prior canary window. Hypothesis: preview flows are hitting a longer sequence length (client debug metadata). Action: add histogram for request.sequence_length to canary telemetry.
- Local dev ergonomics: the fake-canary toggle needs to work with local dev server (so product demos can show canary). Liam will add a dev-only query param that simulates cohort assignment. Add tests.

Decisions made (quick):
1) Expose rollout_cohort in event schema — Rina to own. Target ship: next telemetry deploy (2026-06-17).
2) MVP UI shows inline fallback banner when fallback happened in last 24h + a link to timeline drilldown. Marcus to produce design micro-spec by EOD 6/15.
3) Budget: temporary increase in metric retention to 14d for canary cohorts to give analytics enough samples; product OK'd on temporary cost. Jae to confirm on-call alert thresholds.

Blocking items / risks:
- Auth: PR #482 is blocked by auth shim mismatch with dedicated deployments (missing audit headers). Need SRE help. Ticket INF-2420 assigned to SRE (cc: @sre-oncall).
- Metrics noise: early canary was noisy — sampling rate is inconsistent across regions. Could bias apple-to-apple comparisons. Short-term fix: force sampling=1 for canary cohort (only for 24h windows). Long-term: sampling harmonization pipeline.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Rina: file the schema change ticket INF-2411 for rollout_cohort + add docs to Confluence. ETA: 2026-06-15.
- Marcus: design micro-spec + screenshots for inline fallback banner. Blocked by auth shim for full end-to-end. ETA: 2026-06-15 (mockups)
- Liam: add local fake-cohort query param, unit test, and update dev readme. PR target: 2026-06-16.
- Jae: validate alert thresholds, confirm temporary 14d retention — coordinate with finance. ETA: 2026-06-16.
- Priya: schedule 15m dry run with Solutions Eng for next canary (2026-06-18). Also will prepare short demo script.

Quick observations / heuristics we talked through:
- Canary windows should be short (3–6 hours) for UI-driven experiments to limit blast radius for frontend regressions.
- Always include a human-in-the-loop check when the canary changes routing policies (not just model params).
- Don't treat metric variance as failure >50% until cohort sizes >1000 requests — statistics note. Rina to add checklist item to the rollout playbook.

Loose brainstormed ideas (parking lot):
- "Playback mode" in the panel: replay canary events for troubleshooting. Could hook into existing recording infra.
- Lightweight A/B diff: show example failing vs passing trace side-by-side for quick triage.
- Canary weight ramp suggestions: suggest ramp schedule based on past p95 variance of the route. Requires a small ML model (maybe simple heuristics first).

Meeting micro-log (timestamps):
- 10:02 quick sync: Marcus shows PR and mockup.
- 10:10: Rina outlines telemetry gaps.
- 10:18: Liam proposes local dev toggle.
- 10:23: Jae on alerts and retention.
- 10:30: wrap.

Follow-ups / where to comment:
- PR conversation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/482 (please add review comments by EOD 6/15)
- Slack thread for the standup: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02CANARY/p1686760000000 (short notes and screen grabs)
- Draft rollout playbook edits: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROLL-frontend-canary-playbook

Notes to self (Priya):
- Remind SE to warm the credentials for demo cluster before dry run.
- Capture a 45s clip of the fallback banner to include in demo mail.

Unresolved questions:
- Are we ok with temporary retention bump cost-wise for all customers or only internal canaries? (Need finance sign-off)
- What is the guardrail for client-side sequence_length manipulation? Could be abused in demos to appear cheaper/more expensive. Need boundary checks.

End of capture. Will update doc after PR moves or schema ticket is filed.

---
Editorial: this doc is intentionally light on formal wording — meant to be a working capture for the console & tooling garage standup. If anything here should be promoted to the rollout playbook, ping me and I will extract it.
